question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $x≡29\,(\text{mod}\,8)?$
question.worked_solution:
When we add zero to both sides of a congruence modulo $n$, we can form an equivalent congruence by writing zero as an integer multiple of $n.$ This works because every integer multiple of $n$ is congruent to zero modulo $n.$

In our case, we add zero to both sides of the congruence and then use the fact that  $8\cdot (-3)≡0\,(\text{mod}\,8)$ to rewrite the right-hand side, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+0 & ≡29+0\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\ x & ≡29+0\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡29+8\cdot (-3)\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡29-24\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡5\, & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$
